summary: Backend-only regression testing of the imported GestorCred app after the main agent's edits (lint cleanups, ObjectId fix, object-storage refactor for uploads/backups). Created /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 23 pytest cases: auth login (field 'senha'), /api/auth/me, protected-route enforcement, clientes & emprestimos paginated listings against the imported data, emprestimo detail + parcelas + 404, dashboard, relatorios PDF/Excel generation, admin_transacoes listing/exportar/exportar-csv/metricas, suporte user+admin tickets & estatisticas, and the full upload -> object-storage -> serve round trip. Result: 23/23 passed, zero 500s, no ObjectId serialization leaks, no import errors in backend logs. Separately exercised the backup flow (non-destructive, restaurar_agora=false) and found one real regression in GET /api/backup/listar.

critical.issue: REGRESSION from the object-storage refactor: after a successful POST /api/backup/importar (restaurar_agora=false) the newly imported backup does NOT appear in /api/backup/listar (returned {backups: [], total: 0, pasta: '/app/backups'}). importar() now writes only to Emergent Object Storage, but listar_backups() still enumerates the local /app/backups directory. Consequence: a user who imports a backup cannot see or select it in the UI to restore/download it. It only becomes visible after GET /api/backup/download/{nome} happens to materialize the file locally via _garantir_backup_local(). Fix: make listar_backups() list objects under '{APP_NAME}/backups/' in object storage (or read from the backup_logs collection) instead of/merged with the local dir.

minor.issue: Metadata is empty for object-storage-backed files: entries come back with criado_em: '' and data_formatada: 'N/A' (only tamanho_bytes populated). Timestamps should be derived from backup_logs.created_at or the storage object metadata.

services/object_storage.py uses the synchronous `requests` library and is called directly from async endpoints (put_object/get_object). These blocking network calls (timeouts up to 120s) block the FastAPI event loop and will stall all other requests under load. Wrap with `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` or use httpx.AsyncClient.

File type validation is extension-only (ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS) with no magic-byte/content sniffing, and the whole file is read into memory before the 5MB size check (await file.read() then len(data) > MAX_FILE_SIZE), so an attacker can force arbitrarily large memory allocation. Enforce the limit via streaming/content-length before buffering.
Not a failure, but note: routes/relatorios.py has a duplicated line `periodo_str = f"..."` computed twice back-to-back (lines ~65 and ~68) - dead code left over from the cleanup.

action_items: Fix GET /api/backup/listar so imported backups stored in object storage are listed (currently only reads local /app/backups) - this breaks the import -> restore user flow.
Populate criado_em/data_formatada for backups sourced from object storage.
Wrap the synchronous object_storage put_object/get_object calls in asyncio.to_thread (or switch to httpx async) so uploads/backups don't block the event loop.
Enforce the 5MB upload limit before buffering the whole file in memory, and add content-type/magic-byte validation.
Remove the duplicated periodo_str assignment in routes/relatorios.py.
critical_code_review_comments: backup.py: importar() persists to object storage only, while listar_backups() reads the local filesystem - the two halves of the refactor are inconsistent, producing the HIGH issue above.

object_storage.py: blocking `requests` I/O invoked from async route handlers; also init_storage() caches a module-global key with no lock, so concurrent first-requests will each POST /init (benign but wasteful) - refresh-on-404 retry logic is good though.

Soft-delete field naming is inconsistent across collections: clientes/emprestimos use `deleted`, routes/upload.py uses `is_deleted`. Verified this is why listings show 37/60 instead of the raw 38/63 admin-owned docs (1 cliente + 3 emprestimos have deleted:true) - correct behaviour, but the naming divergence is a footgun.

admin_transacoes.py registers GET /exportar/{formato} (line ~508) before GET /exportar (line ~899); both resolve correctly today but the split of exportar_transacoes vs exportar_transacoes_json into two overlapping paths is confusing - consider consolidating.
admin_transacoes.py exportar_transacoes_json still contains a 'TODO: Implementar formatação CSV/Excel' and returns JSON regardless of the ?formato param, so ?formato=excel silently returns JSON.

rca_of_the_issue: GET /api/backup/listar returning an empty list after import: the object-storage refactor changed the write path (importar -> put_object('gestorcred/backups/<nome>')) but left the read path (listar_backups()) enumerating the local BACKUP_DIR (/app/backups). Because importar() no longer writes to disk, the directory stays empty and listar returns total:0. Reproduction: POST /api/backup/importar with a .tar.gz and restaurar_agora=false -> 200 {sucesso:true, nome:'backup-importado-...tar.gz'}; then GET /api/backup/listar -> {backups:[], total:0}. Proof of the cause: calling GET /api/backup/download/<nome> succeeds (200, application/gzip, correct bytes) because _garantir_backup_local() pulls the object down to /app/backups, and a subsequent GET /api/backup/listar then shows the entry. Mitigation: implement listing against the object-storage prefix 'gestorcred/backups/' (or the backup_logs collection) and merge with any local files, using backup_logs.created_at for the timestamp fields.
